newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil slumps on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil slumps on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Australian-based beverage and snackfoods company Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) Ltd slumped A$2.32 or 13.2 percent to A$15.22 in early trading after its warning late on Friday that profits in 1996 would be flat.
In August CCA had forecast 10 percent plus profit growth for the calendar year.
The company also said trading results in the past three months had been below budget expectations.

"Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) advised today that the company's aggressive investment programme and accelerated growth strategy have been successful in driving sales volume and market share increase, particularly in developing economies," CCA said in a statement to the stock exchange on Friday.

"This strategy has had cost and profit implications, particularly in Europe, and, given the subdued and cautious retail environment in Australia, directors now believe that the company's net profit result for the year ending December 31,
1996, will show little change with the 1995 reported result," it said.
"In forming this view, directors have taken account of trading results over the last three months, which did not achieve budget expectations," it said.

CCA said in early August after its first half results that it expected calender 1996 profit would be 10 percent or more above the A$138.6 million recorded in calendar 1995. Analysts said they were downgrading their profit forecasts for 1996 and 1997 by as much as 20 percent to around A$140 million.
"I think it's very substantial this warning," said a senior analyst, adding that he was lowering his forecast by around 20 percent.

Analysts said however that CCA's price may have bottomed at just above A$15.00 and many Australian institutions, who are relatively underweight in the stock, could look to buy up stock being dumped by some foreign investors.
"A lot of the negative sentiment is coming out of the United States this morning, so some of the locals could look to buy in here," the senior analyst said.
Another said the warning was a positive step overall and the stock remained a strong growth opportunity as the flat earnings were the result of crucial investment needed for future growth.

"They're going to have three years of minimal profit growth that sets them up for 15 years of abnormal returns," the analyst said. By 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), CCA's share price was down 1.99 at A$15.55. CCA is 40 percent owned by The Coca-Cola Co.
